title: Seed document is prompt, not authority
assumption: The uploaded Missing Half seed document is a generative map and candidate list; individual case mentions remain unverified until source acquisition.
invalidation_triggers: A later revision supplies primary-source-backed records for a seed case.
The user explicitly marks a seed item as already verified and supplies sources.

title: Prior-art cubes teach archive grammar
assumption: The old cubes are useful mainly as structural, procedural, and revision-practice prior art, not as substantive sources about missing-knowledge cases.
invalidation_triggers: A prior-art cube is later designated as a substantive source for this project.

title: Primary-source first promotion
assumption: A factual record should not be promoted above candidate status without at least one primary or high-grade synthesis source and explicit source permanence metadata.
invalidation_triggers: The project admits a special-case exception in a revision receipt.

title: Engineering failures are the easiest first pilot
assumption: Official accident-investigation archives make engineering-failure records the best initial pilot lane because source provenance and causal structure are often explicit.
invalidation_triggers: A different lane yields a cleaner first verified record with less acquisition burden.

title: No wall-of-shame default
assumption: The archive must frame failures as system learning and epistemic correction, not humiliation of researchers, operators, or victims.
invalidation_triggers: Any record style starts naming people as blame tokens without contextual/systemic handling.

title: Linked records beat lists
assumption: The core contribution is not collecting famous failures but linking claims, sources, replications, practice changes, patterns, and genealogy.
invalidation_triggers: A pilot shows list-form alone carries comparable value.

title: Small reentry surfaces matter
assumption: Every revision should remain reopenable by a future LLM or maintainer through compact surfaces before deep documents.
invalidation_triggers: The archive grows beyond current reentry budget and requires a new compressed state format.

title: Claims need status over time
assumption: The same claim can move from positive to null, contested, revived, narrowed, or superseded; records must preserve status history rather than one final label.
invalidation_triggers: A schema revision separates historical and current status into different record families.

title: Denominator graph beats mistake list
assumption: The project's highest value comes from linking denominators, status histories, source permanence, practice lag, and transmission paths, not from compiling isolated examples of wrong claims.
invalidation_triggers: A pilot shows that list-like records deliver most user value without graph machinery.
The graph layer becomes too expensive to maintain relative to evidence quality.

title: Pattern records should be downstream
assumption: Recurring pattern records should not be promoted until multiple sourced case records justify the recurrence.
invalidation_triggers: A domain has an official taxonomy of patterns that can be adopted as source-backed pattern authority before case ingestion.

title: Official report is strong but not complete
assumption: An official investigation report is sufficient to promote a bounded incident shell, but not sufficient to call the case historically complete or causally final.
invalidation_triggers: The project decides promotion requires multi-source historical synthesis, not a primary-source shell.
A promoted record starts suppressing unknowns and counter-sources.

title: Patterns remain provisional after three cases
assumption: Three promoted cases can justify a pattern candidate but not a stable theory of recurrence, frequency, or prevention.
invalidation_triggers: A later pattern review admits a more formal threshold.
A pattern record gets used without negative controls.

title: Program-level replication records can be first-class when child records are not yet extracted
assumption: A replication initiative such as the Reproducibility Project: Psychology can be promoted as a program-level record if it clearly states its grain, preserves multiple replication metrics, and refuses to stand in for all child study-pair records.
invalidation_triggers: A later pass shows the program-level record obscures important heterogeneity in a way that misleads queries.
Child records are created and reveal that the program summary should be demoted to a synthesis-only surface.

title: Hard-endpoint reversal pattern is useful but not mature
assumption: WHI, CAST, SELECT, and CARET are enough to seed a pattern candidate about plausible positive proxy routes failing under hard endpoints, but not enough to estimate frequency, assign blame, or declare all proxy evidence weak.
invalidation_triggers: A second review finds one of the four cases is misclassified.
Negative controls show the pattern is too broad without subfamilies.
A stronger synthesis separates surrogate-endpoint, observational-confounding, nutrient-dose, and risk-benefit-profile failures.

title: Genealogy edges are typed relations, not causal proof
assumption: A formal advisor edge, a workshop co-presence edge, a citation, and a reaction-against edge each require distinct source and confidence handling; none by itself proves broad intellectual influence.
invalidation_triggers: A later schema successfully separates influence from genealogy so strongly that this assumption becomes redundant.
A record uses co-presence or formal lineage as causal influence without source support.

title: Program-audit records are historical verdicts under defined criteria
assumption: ALPAC and Lighthill should be encoded as evaluator reports with mandates, criteria, negative/narrowing findings, preserved recommendations, and downstream uncertainty, not as timeless verdicts about machine translation or AI.
invalidation_triggers: A later review finds that program-audit records should be treated only as historiography rather than negative-result records.
A program-audit record loses its preserved-work fields and becomes a slogan.

title: Later revival does not erase earlier negative result
assumption: Modern success in a domain can coexist with an earlier source-backed negative result if the earlier result is scoped to its time, criteria, technology, data, and practical target.
invalidation_triggers: A later archival policy decides that revived domains should be represented only as status-history records, not negative-result records.

title: Warnings are first-class evidence, not just prelude to final causes
assumption: For engineering failures, the cube should preserve pre-event warning signals, where they landed, who had authority to act, and how they were neutralized or converted into action; otherwise incident records become post-hoc cause summaries that hide the missing knowledge transfer.
invalidation_triggers: A later record design captures warning flow better without a distinct warning-governance field.
Second-pass review shows rev0006 warning fields encourage hindsight bias more than learning.

title: Proof-burden inversion is a candidate pattern, not a verdict
assumption: Challenger, Columbia, Boeing 737 MAX, and BP Texas City are enough to make proof-burden/weak-warning-authority visible as a candidate pattern, but not enough to estimate frequency or assign generic blame.
invalidation_triggers: Negative controls show the four cases do not share a useful structure.
A source review demotes one or more case records.
A mature synthesis splits the candidate into unrelated subfamilies.

title: Severe famous disasters are biased training data
assumption: The first warning-governance cases are famous fatal disasters with unusually rich reports; they are valuable for schema formation but biased for pattern frequency and should be balanced by near-misses, stopped-work cases, and false alarms.
invalidation_triggers: Future sampling design demonstrates that famous-disaster-first did not distort pattern formation.
A broad near-miss corpus produces different warning-governance fields.

title: Reporting infrastructure is not effectiveness evidence
assumption: A confidential or voluntary reporting system can be promoted as source infrastructure without claiming that it captures a complete denominator, changes outcomes, or closes actions well.
invalidation_triggers: Future source review finds no durable reporting pathway or shows promoted pages misstate current operation.
Outcome records demonstrate enough action closure to support an upgraded effectiveness claim.

title: De-identified report import requires separate privacy protocol
assumption: Even public de-identified narratives can become re-identifiable when cross-linked; rev0007 therefore promotes infrastructures but imports no individual report narratives.
invalidation_triggers: A privacy review defines safe aggregation and redaction rules for report imports.
A source explicitly licenses specific narratives for reproduction and the cube adopts anti-reidentification constraints.

title: Visibility rails are link classes, not truth verdicts
assumption: Registry records, preregistrations, Registered Reports, retraction metadata, and PubPeer comments should be represented as typed links attached to claims/studies, not as automatic determinations of validity, invalidity, misconduct, completion, or nonpublication.
invalidation_triggers: A later schema can encode these distinctions more precisely and retire this assumption.
A record treats a PubPeer comment, preregistration, or registry absence as a verdict without independent source support.

title: A denominator infrastructure record can be promoted before a denominator audit
assumption: The cube can promote the existence and design of visibility infrastructure before estimating its coverage or compliance, provided every record states that visibility is partial and not an effectiveness/completeness claim.
invalidation_triggers: Future users repeatedly misread infrastructure records as coverage claims despite warnings.
Compliance audits show a promoted platform has changed or ceased operation so much that the infrastructure record needs demotion or reclassification.

title: Audit-pair records reveal missing denominators better than visible-literature lists
assumption: For file-drawer work, the cube should privilege records that compare a denominator surface (protocol, registry, regulator, inception cohort) with a published numerator surface, rather than simply listing famous unpublished/null cases.
invalidation_triggers: A future lane finds important domains where no denominator surface can exist but robust missing-result records can still be built.
A mature schema gives equal or better confidence to another source-acquisition method.

title: Publication-bias audits are not misconduct verdicts
assumption: Nonpublication, delayed publication, outcome switching, and nontransparent reporting are evidence-system states; author/sponsor/journal motive requires separate source support.
invalidation_triggers: A record infers misconduct from a reporting gap without direct source evidence.
A legal/regulatory finding supplies source-backed intent or misconduct for a specific child record.

title: Software failure is not synonymous with cybersecurity vulnerability
assumption: The software/IT lane must distinguish operational outage, deployment failure, monitoring blindness, vulnerability exposure, exploitation, breach, and post-incident investigation because each has different evidence and ethics.
invalidation_triggers: A later schema replaces these distinctions with a better ontology without collapsing them.
A record treats a CVE/NVD/KEV entry as sufficient evidence of incident cause or patch state.

title: Vendor postmortems are useful but provenance-limited
assumption: For software incidents without an accident-board report, vendor PIR/RCA sources may support a one-pass record only if provenance is explicit and independent follow-up remains open.
invalidation_triggers: An independent regulator/board report becomes available and contradicts the vendor account.
The cube adopts a stricter policy that vendor sources cannot promote incident records without official corroboration.

title: Vulnerability rails are not software-incident rails
assumption: CVE, NVD, and CISA KEV make vulnerability negative-space visible, but they do not capture the full denominator of software operational failures, outages, silent alarms, bad rollouts, or recovery failures.
invalidation_triggers: A future official infrastructure provides comprehensive public software incident investigation and recommendation tracking.
An audit shows a vulnerability rail has been systematically extended into incident causal investigation, requiring reclassification.

title: Software accountability records require attribution-surface separation
assumption: For cases where software becomes evidence against people, patients, regulators, or the public, the cube should separate internal state, external symptoms, attribution process, investigation rail, and correction surface before synthesizing a pattern.
invalidation_triggers: A future schema replaces these fields with a better machine-testimony ontology.
A record collapses technical defect, legal blame, and public harm into a single undifferentiated claim.

title: Horizon source status is not final-causal complete
assumption: Post Office Horizon Inquiry Volume 1 supports human-impact/redress and institutional-knowledge claims, but the full causal/governance inquiry record is not complete at rev0011.
invalidation_triggers: Later inquiry volumes publish and supersede the interim boundary.

title: Replication records are boundary maps
assumption: Multi-lab replication records should preserve protocol, population, setting, lab ecology, effect estimate, uncertainty, and outcome class instead of collapsing into did/did-not replicate verdicts.
invalidation_triggers: A future schema provides a more precise record grain taxonomy.

title: Successful controls are required
assumption: A corpus of failed replications must also encode robust or successful-control replications, otherwise it teaches only absence and cannot calibrate what durable knowledge looks like.
invalidation_triggers: The project creates a separate positive-control corpus with explicit links back into this cube.

title: Practice-lag sample opens pattern but does not mature it
assumption: The four selected medical cases are enough to open but not mature a practice-lag/de-adoption pattern candidate.
risk: The cases may differ too much by specialty, comparator, and de-adoption mechanism.
followthrough: Add adoption curves, guideline histories, coverage histories, and utilization child records before upgrading MKH-PAT-0013.

title: Correction rails are not primary evidence
assumption: Infrastructure records such as Choosing Wisely, Cochrane, GRADE, NICE, and EBI can be useful correction surfaces without being treated as primary evidence.
risk: Confusing method/guideline/conversation rails with trial evidence could overstate certainty or jurisdiction.
followthrough: Add explicit evidence-class and jurisdiction fields to future infrastructure schema revisions.

title: earned capability is better than count
assumption: Future usefulness will correlate more strongly with earned capabilities and review depth than with raw record count.
invalidation_triggers: Users primarily need broad lookup coverage before depth
review passes stall useful expansion
capability framework becomes performative bureaucracy

title: current schemas are provisional
assumption: Current record types are useful enough for seed work but should not constrain the 10k+ revision future.
invalidation_triggers: Schema changes break auditability
too much flexibility causes inconsistent records
future sessions cannot compare records across lanes
